P1.findings_md:
WHAT WE SEE — DIGITAL STRATEGY (: 2.77): Robert Entin has served as CIO since 2006 — 18 years in role, an extraordinary tenure in commercial real estate where CIO turnover typically runs every 4–6 years. Entin founded property management software company IBS in 1979, onboarded VNO as a client, and ultimately joined VNO's leadership team directly [E-103]. His technology philosophy — documented in a 2024 VTS interview — is the 'best-of-breed wheel': each business function served by the market-leading point solution, integrated through common data flows [E-088]. Named PropTech Power 30 in both 2022 and 2023 [E-091] and teaching real estate technology at Columbia University, Entin's digital leadership is genuine and above the peer median (: 2.79 vs. peer 2.50). The development area is the absence of a formal CDO and a published IT roadmap — both governance deficits that limit the institutional continuity of the digital strategy beyond any single leader.
WHAT WE SEE — GOVERNANCE (: 2.36): VNO's Board maintains an Audit Committee that oversees cybersecurity risk, and the 2026 Proxy DEF 14A [E-075] documents a formal governance framework with committee charters. Deloitte & Touche LLP has maintained SOX 404(b) attestation without material weaknesses through the 2025 audit year [E-073]. However, the CIO dual-hatted model — Entin simultaneously leading IT strategy, cybersecurity oversight, and application management — is atypical for a $6.8B public company. There is no Chief Data Officer. The VP Security Engineering reports to the CIO rather than as an independent function [E-108, E-110]. (2.36) is below the peer median (2.70) and below the 2.5 threshold that triggers the connected cap: all P3 categories are capped at level 3.0 as a result. The absence of a CDO is not a title deficiency — it is a data governance deficiency with measurable maturity consequences.
WHAT WE SEE — ESG (: 4.04 — HIGHEST-SCORING CATEGORY IN THE ASSESSMENT): In January 2025, VNO became the first major US REIT to achieve 100% LEED certification across its entire portfolio [E-034]. The 2026 Sustainability Report confirms GHG reductions of 70% — ahead of the SBTi-committed 64% by 2030 [E-098]. GRESB 5-star designation and Green Star recognition for 13 consecutive years place VNO in the top 3% of global real estate companies on sustainability metrics. The Energy Information Portal (EIP) — VNO's proprietary IoT platform deployed in 2009 — connects 3,000 submeters across 17M SF to real-time energy dashboards [E-095]. The $750M green bond issued in 2022 is covenant-linked to these outcomes. This is not just leading practice — it is the definitive ESG benchmark for US commercial REITs, sitting 0.94 points above the peer median and above Boston Properties (3.5), the widely cited ESG leader in gateway-city office real estate.
WHAT WE SEE — INNOVATION & CULTURE (: 2.34 |: 2.60): Entin hosts the MetaPropCast podcast, serves on the Realcomm Advisory Board, and participated as a subject matter expert in the Northspyre webinar on development operations automation [E-069, E-091]. Employee sentiment confirms a positive cultural environment: Glassdoor overall 4.1/5 (106 reviews), CEO approval 85.88%, 93% recommend to a friend [E-041]. Innovation culture is above average for a REIT employer. The scoring reflects genuine level 2-Developing capability — strong signals of CIO innovation leadership, less clear evidence of formal innovation programs, R&D investment, or structured experimentation beyond the PropTech vendor evaluation pipeline.
WHY IT MATTERS — STRATEGIC IMPLICATION: P1's ESG strength (4.04) is a revenue mechanism, not a compliance cost. LEED 100% and WELL Health-Safety certifications are increasingly required by the corporate tenants VNO competes for; at >$100/SF average initial rents [E-031], tenants are choosing a sustainability brand as much as a location. However, SVP Paciorek's team is producing the 17th consecutive sustainability report through manual data aggregation from ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager, EIP, GRESB, GRI, and external assurance providers. The Zennify recommendation is to automate this pipeline via Net Zero Cloud — preserving the ESG leadership position while eliminating the manual reporting bottleneck and producing tenant-facing ESG scorecards as a leasing differentiator.
P1.heading: Pillar 1: Strategy, Governance & Culture — 2.82/5.0 vs. Peer Median 2.70

P2.findings_md:
WHAT WE SEE — CRM (: 1.18 — MOST CRITICAL DEVELOPMENT AREA): VTS was deployed in 2011 as a leasing pipeline management tool [E-049]. Fifteen years later, it remains VNO's primary — and only — system for tracking tenant activity. VTS is a transaction system: it records lease negotiations, expiration dates, and square footage. It is not a CRM: it does not capture relationship history, expansion signals, sentiment data, or cross-portfolio tenant behavior. CIO Entin confirmed this architecture in a 2024 interview, positioning VTS as the leasing system of record alongside Box (content) and HqO (experience) [E-088] — none of which provide CRM functionality. VNO manages 3,000+ active tenants across 26M SF of premium Manhattan office without a single field capturing 'what is the probability this tenant exercises their expansion option?' or 'when did we last meet with this tenant's CFO?'
The financial consequence of the CRM gap is most visible in VNO's TI economics. Tenant improvement costs average $148 per square foot, or 13.4% of initial rent [E-042]. At this cost, the economics of tenant retention are decisive: losing a 50,000 SF tenant costs approximately $7.4M in TI alone before factoring in vacancy and re-leasing concessions. The $125M incremental NOI targeted from PENN 1 and PENN 2 lease-up by 2027 depends on retaining and expanding existing tenants. Yet VNO's leasing team has no proactive platform to identify which of the 3,000+ tenants are most likely to churn, no automated renewal trigger workflow, and no cross-portfolio visibility into tenant expansion patterns. scores 1.18 — below even Equity Commonwealth (estimated 1.5), the cash-preservation-mode peer that has deliberately divested most of its portfolio.
WHAT WE SEE — FIELD SERVICE (: 1.88): Building Maintenance Services LLC (BMS), VNO's wholly-owned subsidiary, operates 2,725 field associates providing engineering, janitorial, security, and architectural maintenance across VNO's NYC, Chicago, and San Francisco portfolio [E-078]. These associates use three separate systems: Corrigo for CMMS work order management, Angus Anywhere for tenant service request intake, and Blueforce for field tracking [E-071]. There is no unified dispatch queue, no SLA dashboard, and no cross-system visibility. A maintenance supervisor at PENN 1 cannot view all open work orders from a single screen. A tenant submitting a service request through the TSC web portal cannot see a real-time status update once dispatched to BMS field operations. The connected cap also applies: Data Governance (2.34) is below 2.5, capping at level 3.0 — meaning FSL cannot achieve its full potential without a concurrent Data Cloud deployment.
WHAT WE SEE — TENANT EXPERIENCE & MARKETING (: 2.14 |: 1.48): PENN 1 was awarded the global HqO Best Spaces certification — the first building in the world to receive this designation [E-064]. The HqO REX platform (Real Estate Experience) is deployed across the VNO portfolio for tenant app functionality and experience analytics [E-065]. These are genuine level 2-level 3 capability signals. However, the HqO experience exists alongside three other tenant-facing systems (Box Hub for lease documents, TSC portal for service requests, LIVE.WORK.DO app for building information) — four separate touchpoints with four separate logins, no unified tenant identity, and no cross-platform data flow. Digital marketing (: 1.48) has no marketing automation of any kind; tenant acquisition is entirely inbound, no campaigns, no lead nurture, no ABM.
WHY IT MATTERS — STRATEGIC IMPLICATION: P2 scores 1.67 — the lowest pillar in the assessment and the single largest contributor to pulling VNO's overall score below level 3. P2 carries 30% weight in the Asset Management sub-vertical precisely because the client/tenant journey is the primary revenue mechanism for a commercial REIT. Addressing (Sales Cloud) and (FSL) alone would lift the overall score by approximately 0.4 points. The connected interaction makes Data Cloud the prerequisite: without entity-resolved tenant identity from Data Cloud, FSL cannot reach level 3.5+ capability. Zennify sells Sales Cloud + Data Cloud + FSL as a unified platform — not as sequential point solutions — because the maturity math requires all three to move together.
P2.heading: Pillar 2: Client & Tenant Journey — 1.67/5.0 vs. Peer Median 2.40 — The Platform Gap That Defines VNO's Digital Ceiling

P3.findings_md:
WHAT WE SEE — COMPLIANCE (: 2.78 — ABOVE PEER): VNO's formal compliance framework is its strongest operational domain after ESG. SOX 404(b) attestation is maintained by Deloitte & Touche without material weaknesses [E-073]. The 2026 DEF 14A confirms Audit Committee oversight of cybersecurity, financial reporting, and compliance [E-075]. OFAC and EAR compliance are explicitly documented in Terms & Conditions [E-074]. CCPA multi-state privacy compliance is formalized. Local Law 97 (NYC carbon law) compliance is achieved through LEED 100% certification — VNO is ahead of the penalty curve and a leader among NYC commercial landlords [E-076]. (3.07) is above the peer median (3.20 is aspirational BXP benchmark; VNO is proximate). The Zennify opportunity in compliance is automation rather than remediation.
WHAT WE SEE — FRAUD MANAGEMENT (: 1.83 — CAPPED level 2): The Solomon conviction is the most significant event in this assessment. Jared Solomon served as VP Leasing for 14–16 years. He created two fictitious brokerage entities — Margoux Media and Cobalt Advisors — submitted invoices for non-existent services, and collected $9.5M over the course of a decade and a half [E-072]. The jury required 90 minutes to deliberate. EVP Glen Weiss testified that he trusted Solomon completely. The specific control that was absent: no automated vendor ownership verification was required before processing broker commission payments. The broker disclosure requirement existed in leasing agreements — Solomon disclosed the fake brokerages on lease forms — but that disclosure was not programmatically cross-referenced against vendor ownership records. VNO is the victim party. The control gap is not a character failure; it is a platform gap.
WHAT WE SEE — AUTOMATION (: 2.45): VNO has implemented meaningful workflow automation at the content layer. Box Relay enables automated invoice routing, lease document management, and approval workflows [E-087]. Northspyre, deployed in 2025, automates development project budgets, bid analysis, and contract tracking [E-069, E-070]. These are genuine level 2-level 3 automation capabilities. However, there is no confirmed enterprise RPA, and API integrations between the 17+ technology stack vendors appear to be point-to-point. The absence of MuleSoft or equivalent iPaaS means each new system integration requires custom development — a technical debt that compounds as the stack grows.
WHAT WE SEE — RESILIENCE & TPRM (: 2.71 — CAPPED level 3): CIO Entin has documented a formal 4-gate vendor evaluation process: cyber posture, database soundness, data integration fit, and stakeholder readiness [E-079]. This process is executed manually for each new vendor evaluation. VNO's offices remained open throughout the COVID-19 pandemic — BMS 24/7 operations and building infrastructure continuity were maintained without material disruption [E-082]. Active litigation (PENN 1 ground rent), maturity defaults ($319M), and the JV default ($800M non-recourse) are MATERIAL issues capping at level 3.0, but VNO's $2.4B liquidity provides a resilience buffer [E-080].
WHY IT MATTERS — STRATEGIC IMPLICATION: The P3 paradox is that compliance infrastructure strength (SOX 404(b), Audit Committee, OFAC, CCPA) did not prevent a 14-year, $9.5M fraud by a trusted VP. This is the difference between formal compliance and operational controls. The August 4, 2026 sentencing is a board-level attention event. Zennify's Shield + Compliance Workflows is positioned as remediation — automated broker ownership verification, dual-approval for commissions over $50K, conflict-of-interest attestation, and SOX-grade audit trail. Deployed before sentencing, it creates documented remediation evidence that could enable a cap lift from S3 (level 2 max) to S2 (level 3 max) in the next assessment cycle.
P3.heading: Pillar 3: Operations, Risk & Compliance — 2.44/5.0 vs. Peer Median 2.78 — Compliance Strength Masking an Operational Controls Development Area

P4.findings_md:
WHAT WE SEE — DATA GOVERNANCE (: 2.34): Box was deployed in 2019 as VNO's enterprise SSOT [E-087]. Box Governance enforces retention and policy; Box Shield provides DLP and classification; Box Vera adds file-level encryption for external collaboration. This is a sophisticated content governance stack for a commercial REIT. However, tenant data is not unified. VTS holds leasing data; Box holds lease documents; HqO holds experience data; TSC holds service requests. Each system has its own tenant record. There is no MDM platform resolving these into unified identity, and no CDO to own the data governance roadmap [E-088]. (2.34) below 2.5 triggers the connected cap on (field service) at level 3.0 — FSL cannot reach its full potential without a concurrent Data Cloud deployment.
WHAT WE SEE — ANALYTICS & AI (: 2.35): VNO's analytics foundation is Microsoft SSRS/SSAS/SSIS, deployed in 2010 and still in production [E-089, E-094]. CIO Entin confirmed in a 2024 interview that the automated earnings model built on this stack runs with 'very little human intervention' [E-094] — genuine level 3 automation on an aging platform. Microsoft is ending SSRS as a new product in SQL Server 2025, creating a forced migration window. On AI: Entin's specific use case — 'Who in the Penn District has expansion options in 2026?' — is a RAG pipeline against Box lease documents [E-093]. He called it 'potentially transformative' and 'a game changer.' Every phrasing is future tense. The enterprise AI platform does not yet exist.
WHAT WE SEE — ARCHITECTURE (: 2.50): The best-of-breed wheel has produced a stable, 18-year architecture with clear integration patterns [E-103]. ERP serves as financial and contract golden record; VTS is leasing pipeline; Box is content SSOT; HqO is tenant experience. IoT is a genuine strength: EIP connects 3,000 submeters across 17M SF, producing real-time energy data [E-095]. Infrastructure spans DigitalOcean Droplets (IaaS, 2020 [E-105]), Amazon CloudFront (CDN), and Microsoft IIS. There is no confirmed enterprise iPaaS — integrations are point-to-point API connections — and the absence of MuleSoft means each new system integration is custom-built.
WHAT WE SEE — CYBERSECURITY (: 2.85 — AT PEER MEDIAN): The 2025 10-K Item 1C discloses a multi-element cybersecurity program: Audit Committee oversight, TPRM, incident response plan (IRP), security training, and continuous monitoring [E-108]. Box Shield and Box Vera provide enterprise-grade content DLP and file-level encryption [E-109]. VP Security Engineering role confirmed via ZoomInfo (2026), reporting to CIO [E-110]. No CISO in the org chart — cybersecurity is an IT function, not an independent strategic discipline. No data breaches or CISA disclosures found in any public source [E-110, negative search confirmed]. (2.85) is marginally above the peer median (2.80) — cybersecurity is one of VNO's most competitive P4 domains.
WHY IT MATTERS — STRATEGIC IMPLICATION: The AI gap in is the most strategically accessible P4 development area, because the CIO has already done the hard work: he identified the use case (lease expansion Q&A), named the data source (Box), and signaled the business value ('game changer') [E-093]. The gap is the AI execution layer. Box AI alone cannot answer 'Who in the Penn District has expansion options in 2026?' — that requires tenant context (Sales Cloud: who is the tenant, what is their account history), not just document search. Agentforce over Data Cloud provides the missing context layer. Tableau migrates the CIO's automated earnings model from the sunsetting SSRS platform to a modern, self-service BI foundation. Together, Tableau + Agentforce delivers the CIO's stated vision with enterprise-grade architecture — Zennify positions this as executing the CIO's own roadmap, not replacing it.
P4.heading: Pillar 4: Technology, Data & Security — 2.51/5.0 vs. Peer Median 2.75 — Stable Architecture; Aging Analytics; AI Vision Without Platform
